transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Try to avoid heavy work or lifting for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops or eye treatment before your operation, like for dry eyes, it is safe to continue using them unless you have been told otherwise.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
A bit of light sensitivity can be normal while your eyes adjust. If it’s mild and things just seem brighter, you can wear sunglasses outside.

But significant pain in bright light, or severe light sensitivity, is not normal, especially if the eye is also red and painful. If that’s happening, we may need to assess it further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly over time.

If it’s still blurry, or getting more blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that covers everything I wanted to ask. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you so much for your assistance!
